1: Each standard integral is the reverse of a standard derivative, so knowing the derivatives gives the integrals. Recognising the pattern is the skill being tested.
2: The chain rule gives d/dx ln|f(x)| = f′(x)/f(x), so integrating f′(x)/f(x) reverses it to ln|f(x)| plus a constant.
3: Differentiating [f(x)]^(n+1)/(n+1) gives f′(x)[f(x)]ⁿ by the chain rule, so the integral follows by reversal. The restriction n ≠ −1 is the case covered by the logarithm rule.
4: Powers of sine and cosine do not integrate directly. Identities rewrite them as sums of simpler trigonometric terms, which can be integrated.
5: Integration loses the constant, so a point on the curve selects the particular solution. Substituting the point into the integral fixes c.
